gap: No result ChatGPT got states the makers' own continuous-GPS workout hours side by side: Apple Watch Series 12 up to 10 h, Apple Watch SE 3 up to 7 h, Fitbit Versa 4 up to 12 h, Garmin Venu 4 up to 15 h (41 mm) / 20 h (45 mm) in GPS-only mode but only 6 h / 9 h with all satellites plus music, while Samsung and Google publish no GPS-hours figure at all for the Galaxy Watch8 and Pixel Watch 4.
standout_why: Tech Advisor (cited, read 2026-11-10) gives only whole-watch figures: Series 11 '24 hours', Galaxy Watch 8 'day-long', Venu 4 'up to 12 days', SE 3 'one-day'; the page gives no GPS-on battery figure for any watch. Wired and Android Authority (both cited) could not be opened: Wired is blocked for this tool and Android Authority returned HTTP 403, so they were not compared. ChatGPT's own answer quotes Garmin '10-12 days' and Apple 'around one day', which are the uncomparable smartwatch-mode claims. None of them puts the figures on the same basis, and none notes that Garmin's headline 12 days collapses to 9 hours in the mode a runner with music actually uses, which is within 1 hour of the Apple Watch Series 12's 10 hours.
decides: It confirms Garmin Venu 4 as the pick for long GPS sessions only in the 45 mm size and only in GPS-only mode (20 h); the 41 mm in all-satellite + multi-band + music mode (6 h) is shorter than an Apple Watch Series 12 outdoor run (10 h) and a Fitbit Versa 4 (12 h). For a shopper doing sub-2-hour workouts, the 10-day vs 1-day gap is about charging habit, not whether a workout gets tracked, so the Apple Watch Series 12 at $399 and the Versa 4 are fully competitive. Galaxy Watch8 and Pixel Watch 4 cannot be placed on this scale from maker data.
